Original underwater fish video: reproducible source-annotation walkthrough

Source: vignettes/articles/real-fish-data-walkthrough.Rmd
real-fish-data-walkthrough.Rmd

Real underwater video: original-source workflow

This walkthrough uses the DIGI4ECO Underwater Fish Tracking Dataset, archived at DOI 10.5281/zenodo.20701225 under CC BY 4.0. The original dataset includes underwater MP4 videos and source-author CVAT 1.1 track annotations. You must credit the dataset creators and identify modifications when using the data.

No original third-party video or annotations are copied into AquaTrajectories or redistributed by its website. Download the files directly from the original Zenodo record. The instructions below operate locally and produce source-labelled observation tables, not model predictions or independently evaluated performance.

Step 1 — Acquire and preserve original media

Select one source sequence, for example the smaller OBSEA recording, and retain the downloaded original video.mp4 and annotations.xml. Record the Zenodo version and the dataset licence.

Use FFmpeg/ffprobe to extract the decoded frame presentation timestamp rather than manufacturing time from frame index and nominal FPS:

ffprobe -v error -select_streams v:0 \
  -show_entries frame=best_effort_timestamp_time \
  -of csv=p=0 "OBSEA/video.mp4" > "OBSEA/source_pts.csv"

The converter requires one valid, strictly increasing raw PTS value for every decoded frame. Failed timestamp checks should trigger investigation of the original recording; never interpolate missing source timing evidence to force a valid audit.

Step 2 — Convert original CVAT tracks, retaining provenance

From an AquaTrajectories repository checkout:

python3 scripts/convert_digi4eco_cvat.py \
  --video "OBSEA/video.mp4" \
  --annotations "OBSEA/annotations.xml" \
  --pts "OBSEA/source_pts.csv" \
  --output "local_outputs/OBSEA" \
  --session "DIGI4ECO_OBSEA" \
  --camera "CAM1"

The standard-library converter writes:

Local output Contents and limitations
source_frames.csv Original frame IDs, raw decoded PTS, recording-relative time, source video dimensions
source_2d_tracks.csv Camera-local source CVAT fish IDs, annotation-box centres, observed/missing rows and original occlusion flags
reviewed_source_boxes.csv Original source-author labels and fish bounding boxes; not AquaTrajectories detections
provenance.json Video, XML and PTS SHA-256 digests; source counts; explicit scientific validity flags

An annotation with outside=1 becomes an unobserved row with blank position coordinates. An annotation with occluded=1 remains flagged; the converter does not silently discard partially visible animals. Original track IDs are preserved as source annotation IDs, not certified biological identities.

Step 3 — Review original video and annotation coordinates

Open the local research data inspector and select source_2d_tracks.csv for original-data timestamp and missingness checks.

You may also open the local multiview evidence desk. For this single-camera example, choose source_frames.csv under frame manifest, source_2d_tracks.csv under 2D tracks, and the original video.mp4 in Camera A. Leave Camera B and source XYZ blank. This is a review of original video and original annotations, not stereo reconstruction or validation of a software detector.

Browser video seeking can land near presentation timestamps, depending on codec and media playback behavior. No browser timestamp alignment proves physical shutter synchronization.

Step 4 — Separate real source evidence from algorithmic inference

These files contain genuine recorded fish observations and source-author annotations. They do not contain predictions from AquaTrajectories, YOLO or ByteTrack. Do not calculate F1, HOTA or IDF1 by comparing the source labels against themselves.

An independent computational benchmark would additionally need frozen detector/tracker predictions, matching rules, reviewed source annotations and sufficiently independent holdout recordings. An underwater XYZ benchmark would separately require a calibrated multiview setup and physically surveyed targets; the DIGI4ECO source labels alone cannot certify underwater XYZ.

Step 5 — Verify the converter and document attribution

Run the converter’s automated structural test:

python3 scripts/test_convert_digi4eco_cvat.py

This test uses invented three-frame CVAT fixture records, not the published DIGI4ECO video. It checks occlusion, outside/missingness, original PTS and provenance handling. Running it does not constitute a real-video model benchmark. The genuine data-processing command above must be run separately after acquiring the original media; the website CI does not download third-party videos.

Cite the original data: DIGI4ECO Underwater Fish Tracking Dataset (2026), original dataset authors, CC BY 4.0.

Cite the software: AquaTrajectories v0.1.1.
